conventions.convention: The DAG is finite and nonempty with a specified topological order. All vertices are observed, structural functions are continuous Borel functions, and the noises are mutually independent with strictly positive Lebesgue densities. Nondescendants exclude the vertex itself.
Causal minimality means that every parent coordinate is essential at some setting of the other parent coordinates; roots have no such condition.

Condition 19 requires failure of the displayed differential equation at at least one point where ν''(y−f(x))f'(x) is nonzero. The input and noise densities are strictly positive C³ densities and f is C³.

Restrictedness quantifies over every edge i→j and every conditioning set between the other parents of j and its nondescendants excluding i. Each pair must have a positive finite density conditioning witness satisfying Condition 19, using the stated marginal-ratio density versions.

RESIT uses a fixed total order for ties and loops, returns failure if Phase 1 has no accepted candidate, and tests pruning residuals against the vector of all preceding vertices. Population consistency is required only for predictor sets containing all parents and contained in the nondescendants.
The RESIT correctness assertion additionally assumes that every Phase 1 regression function is C³ on its full predictor space; it is a population assertion without a finite-sample guarantee.
In the parent-dependence lemma, the symbol ⊥_d denotes an almost-everywhere conditional-density factorization, rather than graphical d-separation.
The Gaussian examples explicitly assume AC, supplying the Countable Choice hypotheses of the normal-density and linear-change suppliers.

load_bearing.statement: A restricted ANM has C³ structural functions and strictly positive C³ noise densities; for every edge and every stated intermediate nondescendant conditioning set, some positive finite conditioning section gives a smooth bivariate model satisfying Condition 19.

Let X,N be independent real random variables, let Y=f(X)+N, and suppose f∈C³(R) is nonconstant while X and N have strictly positive C³ Lebesgue densities. If their triple satisfies Condition 19, there is no reverse representation X=g(Y)+M with M independent of Y and g∈C³(R); no density regularity for M is assumed.

The observational law of a finite additive-noise model has the strictly positive density given by the product, in topological order, of q_j(x_j−f_j(x_pa(j))) relative to finite product Lebesgue measure.

Two finite causally sufficient causally minimal ANMs on distinct DAGs with the same vertices and the same strictly positive observational law have an edge y→l in G reversed as l→y in G', and a set S containing the other parents and contained in the appropriate nondescendants in both graphs.

In a positive-density finite ANM with continuous causally minimal structural functions, every edge i→j remains conditionally dependent given every S with pa(j) excluding i contained in S and S contained in nd(j) excluding i.

If (Y,C) has a strictly positive C³ joint density p and m is C³, independence of R=Y−m(C) and C yields strictly positive C³ marginal density versions satisfying p(y,c)=q_R(y−m(c))p_C(c) at every point.

For an edge y→z with no directed path from z to another child of y, put D equal to the strict descendants of z and S=V excluding D,y,z. The positive joint density factors as A(y,s,z)B(d,s,z), giving conditional independence of X_D and X_y given X_S,X_z, including under every section s with positive finite marginal density.
In a finite ANM, N_j is independent of X_S for every S contained in nd(j).
Let μ be a Borel probability measure on R. If μ(A+a)=μ(A) for every Borel set A, then a=0.

concerns.concern: Proof 5.1 says, in the branch where l is an ancestor of w, that “every path into w ends through a conditioned parent.” This does not cover paths whose final edge is oriented out of w. For example, l→a→w together with l→c←w has such a path l,c,w. The proposed parent separator is nevertheless valid: the omitted paths are blocked by the same first-collider argument used in the other branch, applied from w. The proof should account for that case.
